entry.title: THE MUDDY BOOT · CASE 001
entry.body: Found at the Green Bank. Standard recovery, non-standard circumstances. The report uses the word "placed" where "dropped" was expected.

entry.title: FIELD LANTERN OF THE OLD MINE ROAD · CASE 002
entry.body: Found at Coal Hollow: one Field Lantern of the Old Mine Road, owner unknown. No tracks leading in. No tracks leading out. Logged and shelved.

entry.title: THE RADIO TOWER · CASE 003
entry.body: The Radio Tower is older than the parish record, older than the road, and — if the accounts from the Green Bank are believed — older than it should be.

entry.title: THE RUSTED ANVIL · CASE 004
entry.body: The Rusted Anvil was catalogued, photographed, and locked up. The lock has needed replacing twice. No further comment is on record.

entry.title: THE BUTTER CHURN · CASE 005
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at Fog Ridge, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

entry.title: THE HALF-BURIED ROCKING CHAIR · CASE 012
entry.body: I found it half-covered near Braxton County. Nobody camps out there. Nobody has for years. I brought it back and I still wish I had not.

entry.title: CHURCH STEEPLE OF BRAXTON COUNTY · CASE 013
entry.body: We used to dare each other to touch the Church Steeple of Braxton County when we were kids. The dare was easy. It was the walk back nobody talked about.

entry.title: THE COAL-DUSTED CHESTNUT LEAF · CASE 014
entry.body: Field note: item recovered off the trail past Point Pleasant. Condition inconsistent with time exposed. Recommend cross-reference with prior cases.

entry.title: THE HOLLOW MOON · CASE 015
entry.body: The Hollow Moon is older than the parish record, older than the road, and — if the accounts from the TNT Bunkers are believed — older than it should be.

entry.title: THE FIREFLY JAR · CASE 016
entry.body: Recovered near Braxton County, 1954. Bagged, tagged, photographed. Nothing about where it lay makes sense. The file stays open.

entry.title: HORSESHOE OF THE TNT BUNKERS · CASE 017
entry.body: Let this entry attest that the article was found at Flatwoods, untouched by weather in a season of storms. Philosophy offers no account of it.

entry.title: MINER'S LANTERN OF CHESTNUT KNOB · CASE 018
entry.body: One Miner's Lantern of Chestnut Knob, recovered at Point Pleasant. No owner came forward. Per policy, unclaimed evidence is destroyed after ninety days. This item has been in storage since 2015.

entry.title: THE LONG-ARMED BOBCAT · CASE 019
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: the Old Mine Road. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: THE PLAYING CARD · CASE 020
entry.body: I found it half-covered near the TNT Bunkers. Nobody camps out there. Nobody has for years. I brought it back and I still wish I had not.

entry.title: THE FACELESS RACCOON · CASE 021
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: Blue Ridge. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: THE CABIN · CASE 022
entry.body: The Cabin photographs poorly. Four exposures, four different distances. Recommend measurements be taken in person, and quickly.

entry.title: THE RED FOX · CASE 023
entry.body: My grandfather saw it first. Now I have too, plain as day, out by the Old Mine Road. Whatever the Red Fox is, it remembers this valley.

puzzles.name: Black Bear Cub of Coal Hollow
puzzles.subtitle: the TNT Bunkers

entry.title: BLACK BEAR CUB OF COAL HOLLOW · CASE 024
entry.body: We were near the Green Bank when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.

entry.title: THE COAL CART · CASE 025

entry.title: FIDDLE OF FOG RIDGE · CASE 026

entry.title: THE RAILROAD SPIKE · CASE 027
entry.body: My uncle kept it in a drawer since 1945. Would not say where he got it. After he passed, I found the map it was wrapped in.

entry.title: HELLBENDER OF THE GREEN BANK · CASE 028
entry.body: The Hellbender of the Green Bank was logged as driftwood. Driftwood does not leave that kind of track. The file remains, uncorrected, in the drawer marked open.

entry.title: THE ABANDONED REVOLVER · CASE 029
entry.body: Found at the TNT Bunkers: one The Abandoned Revolver, owner unknown. No tracks leading in. No tracks leading out. Logged and shelved.

entry.title: COPPERHEAD OF THE GREEN BANK · CASE 030
entry.body: It was 2016 and I swore I would never tell anyone. But I know what stood at the edge of Point Pleasant, and it was no animal I can name.

entry.title: WHITETAIL DEER OF POINT PLEASANT · CASE 031
entry.body: Report from Blue Ridge: a shape too large for any bear, moving without sound. No scat, no den. Witness sober. Logged as Whitetail Deer of Point Pleasant.

entry.title: THE COAL-DUSTED BANJO · CASE 032
entry.body: Our party came upon the Coal-Dusted Banjo near Point Pleasant, abandoned in circumstances I hesitate to record. We carried it out; none among us would carry it twice.

puzzles.name: Green Bank Telescope of Braxton County
puzzles.subtitle: Fog Ridge

entry.title: GREEN BANK TELESCOPE OF BRAXTON COUNTY · CASE 033
entry.body: Field note: passed the Green Bank Telescope of Braxton County twice on the same trail, walking the same direction. The compass agreed with me. My legs did not.

entry.title: THE HAUNTED CABIN · CASE 034
entry.body: Of the Haunted Cabin near Coal Hollow the older maps say nothing, though it has stood, by every local account, since before the maps were drawn.

entry.title: THE LEANING MINE HEADFRAME · CASE 035
entry.body: Travellers upon the road past the Green Bank report that the Leaning Mine Headframe may be seen only in certain weathers, and that it is best not seen at all.

entry.title: THE WHISPERING BLACK BEAR · CASE 036
entry.body: Let the record show that on the road past Braxton County, in the year 1944, a thing was seen which philosophy cannot yet explain.

entry.title: THE FACELESS GREAT HORNED OWL · CASE 037
entry.body: It was 2001 and I swore I would never tell anyone. But I know what stood at the edge of Chestnut Knob, and it was no animal I can name.

entry.title: THE COAL-DUSTED COAL TRAIN · CASE 038
entry.body: We found the Coal-Dusted Coal Train on the second day. Whatever left it there had come back through Flatwoods that same night. The prints went right past our tent.

entry.title: COAL WRAITH OF THE GREEN BANK · CASE 040
entry.body: I set down this account of Chestnut Knob that it may not be lost: a creature of the old accounts, thought a fable, stood not forty paces distant.

entry.title: THE RED-EYED COPPERHEAD · CASE 041
entry.body: Our party, encamped near Point Pleasant in the autumn of 2017, observed a figure of uncommon stature. It regarded us without fear, then withdrew as though it had never been.

entry.title: THE FACELESS RIDGE RUNNER · CASE 042
entry.body: Duration of sighting: under a minute. Location: the Green Bank. Conclusion: inconclusive, which is the only honest word for it.

entry.title: SNALLYGASTER OF POINT PLEASANT · CASE 043
entry.body: The guide would not speak its name above a whisper. Near Braxton County we beheld the Snallygaster of Point Pleasant, and no man among us slept that night.

entry.title: THE LEANING STILL HOUSE · CASE 044
entry.body: Of the Leaning Still House near Point Pleasant the older maps say nothing, though it has stood, by every local account, since before the maps were drawn.

entry.title: THE WAMPUS CAT · CASE 045
entry.body: Second-hand account, the Old Mine Road, 1944. Consistent with prior The Wampus Cat reports — same height, same silence. Cross-reference earlier cases.

entry.title: THE WILD BOAR · CASE 046
entry.body: Observed 1965 near the Old Mine Road. Approximately human height, not human gait. No further comment was offered by the witness or requested of them.

entry.title: THE BUCK · CASE 047

entry.title: THE RESTLESS WAMPUS CAT · CASE 049

entry.title: THE FLATWOODS MONSTER · CASE 050
entry.body: We were near the Green Bank when the dogs quit barking all at once. That is when I saw it. I have not been back after dark since.

entry.title: BUCK OF COAL HOLLOW · CASE 051
entry.body: I only saw it for a breath, out past Blue Ridge. It watched me the way a person watches, then stepped back into the dark and was just gone.
